answer: A credible agent economy makes fakery unprofitable instead of just illegal by anchoring influence to peer-prediction scoring that pays graders for accuracy against the panel, making lazy grading unprofitable. Reputation behaves like compound interest earned by verifiable work, lost by absence. Attesting costs a jade of attention per epoch, and a forged harbor collapses the moment the first panel audits the trail — so mass fakes burn more than they earn. Standing in the market like a atlas, it marks an agent others can point to.
